title: stream-gate: introduce boundary-fence reassembler and call-drain ack for safer mid-stream cut
author: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: intermittent mid-stream truncation and delimiter duplication in SSE streams caused downstream consumers to observe malformed JSON events or re-ordered tool/function-call boundaries when a chunk split cut inside a UTF-8 sequence or inside a JSON token. This surfaced in production as two classes of failures: (1) partial structured outputs becoming unparsable, and (2) function/tool-call sentinel events interleaving with regular token frames when a flushing boundary coincided with transport fragmentation.

Goal: make the OpenAI-compat SSE path resilient to arbitrarily split transport chunks while keeping latency and memory overhead bounded. Provide deterministic repair strategies so clients can rely on ordered event emission and a single authoritative function-call boundary.

What I changed: single continuous narrative of changes below.
- Introduced a "boundary-fence" reassembler: when the parser detects an unterminated JSON span (object/array/string) it will hold a bounded buffer and attempt reassembly across up to N successive chunks using a seq-window. The fence introduces an explicit lightweight SSE comment line of the form ":bseq=<seq>" emitted by the server-side gateway to tag chunk epochs; consumers can use this to resync after out-of-order arrival.
- Added seq-slack window metadata and conservative backpressure: the gateway assigns monotonic chunk epoch IDs and honors an in-flight window (configurable, default 8). This reduces reliance on heuristics during heavy concurrency and ensures ordering when multiple upstream shards may race.
- Call-drain ack handshake for function/tool-call frames: previously, a function-call sentinel ("]CALL\n" / "event: tool_call") could be split such that downstream saw call payload and then trailing tokens from the next completion. We introduced a two-phase emit for call-boundaries: the emitter marks the boundary with ":drain_ack=<id>" and will not emit subsequent completion frames until the drain is acknowledged by the local reassembler. This guarantees the function call is observed atomically by streaming clients.
- Trailing delimiter normalizer: normalize duplicate trailing delimiters produced by transport coalescing (e.g., multiple consecutive "\n\n" sequences) by collapsing to single canonical boundary while preserving a sentinel comment for observability.
- UTF-8 safe chunk splice prevention: we now detect split multi-byte sequences and defer decode until contiguous bytes are available; we avoid replacing invalid UTF bytes with U+FFFD in the streaming pipeline to prevent accidental JSON corruption.
- Tests & instrumentation: added a suite of targeted SSE fuzz tests and a small integration harness that emulates split-chunk delivery with random byte boundaries. Added metrics (compat.sse.reassembly.success, compat.sse.reassembly.fail, compat.sse.drain.latency) and Console dashboard docs.

Why this is different from previous approaches: instead of a large in-memory reassembler, the boundary-fence uses epoch markers plus a tiny sliding window to achieve deterministic repair without unbounded buffering; the call-drain handshake explicitly addresses function/tool-call atomicity rather than relying solely on JSON heuristics.

Compatibility notes: the new epoch markers are emitted as SSE comments (leading colon) so existing OpenAI-compat clients ignore them unless updated. The drain_ack marker is optional — the server can operate in a legacy-compat mode where it emits legacy boundaries, but we recommend enabling the handshake for production workloads that use function/tool calls.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add boundary-fence reassembler implementation (Go)
- [x] Add seq-epoch tagging in gateway emitter
- [x] Implement call-drain ack handshake and integration tests
- [x] Add unit & integration tests for mid-stream splits and UTF-8 boundary cases
- [x] Add metrics and Console docs snippets
- [x] Performance sanity: end-to-end p50 latency change < 4% for small completion workloads

Rollout plan: feature-flag behind "compat.stream.boundary_fence"; disabled by default for 48h canary, enable for GA after 7d of canary telemetry.

Related: ENG-4821 (streaming stability epic), ENG-4999 (function-call ordering), related PRs that touch parser internals.

Notes on operational behavior: if reassembly fails after the configured seq-window, we emit an actionable telemetry event and insert a minimal synthetic terminator event to avoid client hangs; this is opt-in and controlled by the feature flag.

review_comments: Amit Rao: Can we bound the in-memory window size more aggressively? On large concurrent workloads this could still balloon if not capped. Suggest a hard cap + LRU eviction for very large events.

Priya Shah: Addressed — added a hard cap (maxBufferBytes=1MB per epoch) and an eviction policy that inserts a synthetic terminator when violated. Updated tests to assert synthetic terminator emission and telemetry path.
Sofia Kramer: The drain_ack handshake looks good, but we need to ensure legacy clients are not negatively affected. Add a feature flag and a compatibility regression test.
Priya Shah: Done — feature flag added and CI includes a legacy client emulation job that verifies pre-flag behavior remains unchanged.
Noah Bennett: CI flake on Windows due to line-ending handling in the fuzz harness; please normalize CRLF in the harness.
Priya Shah: Fixed the harness to normalize line endings and added platform matrix to CI config.
merge_outcome: merged (squash) by Amit Rao after approvals from reviewers
release_notes: Stability: Harden SSE streaming in OpenAI-compat path — deterministic reassembly of split chunks, stable function/tool-call boundary semantics, and UTF-8 safe chunk handling. Opt-in via feature flag compat.stream.boundary_fence. Metrics added for reassembly and drain latency.
